content:
After applying the product-to-sum identity correctly:

\[
\frac12\left(\frac{\cos(\alpha+\beta/2)}{\cos(\alpha-\beta/2)}+1+\frac{\cos(\beta+\alpha/2)}{\cos(\beta-\alpha/2)}+1\right)=1
\]

so

\[
\frac{\cos(\alpha+\beta/2)}{\cos(\alpha-\beta/2)}+\frac{\cos(\beta+\alpha/2)}{\cos(\beta-\alpha/2)}=0.
\]

Using \(\frac{\cos(A+B)}{\cos(A-B)}=\frac{1-\tan A\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}\), let

\[
u=\tan\alpha\tan\frac\beta2,\qquad v=\tan\beta\tan\frac\alpha2.
\]

Then

\[
\frac{1-u}{1+u}+\frac{1-v}{1+v}=0
\]

which gives \(uv=1\). Thus

\[
\tan\alpha\tan\frac\beta2\tan\beta\tan\frac\alpha2=1.
\]

Let \(p=\tan\frac\alpha2,\ q=\tan\frac\beta2\). Then

\[
\frac{2p}{1-p^2}\cdot q\cdot \frac{2q}{1-q^2}\cdot p=1,
\]

so with \(P=p^2,\ Q=q^2\),

\[
P+Q+3PQ=1.
\]

Therefore

\[
\cos\alpha+\cos\beta
=\frac{1-P}{1+P}+\frac{1-Q}{1+Q}
=\frac{2(1-PQ)}{1+P+Q+PQ}.
\]

Since \(P+Q=1-3PQ\),

\[
1+P+Q+PQ=1+(1-3PQ)+PQ=2(1-PQ).
\]

Hence

\[
\cos\alpha+\cos\beta=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
